name: Egg Curry
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi / dhaba-style "anda curry", made in an onion-tomato masala; eaten all over India, with regional cousins such as Kolhapuri anda rassa, Bengali dimer jhol and Kerala mutta curry)

ingredients.name: Water, for boiling the eggs
ingredients.householdMeasure: enough to cover the eggs by 2–3 cm

ingredients.name: Mustard oil (sarson ka tel), or any cooking oil
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (1 tsp for the eggs, 1 tsp for the masala)

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small onion, finely chopped (about ½ cup)

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 medium tomato, finely chopped or grated (about ½ cup)

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder (haldi)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅛ tsp (half for the eggs, half for the masala)

ingredients.name: Salt (namak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅓ tsp (a pinch for the eggs, the rest for the gravy)

ingredients.name: Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp, crushed between the palms

equipment: Small saucepan with a lid, for boiling the eggs
Medium kadai or small heavy-bottomed pan (about 18–20 cm)
Bowl of cold water, for cooling the eggs
Small grater (for ginger, garlic and, if you like, the tomato)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup (a normal teaspoon and a steel glass are fine stand-ins)
Toothpick or fork, for pricking the eggs

steps.title: Put the eggs in water
steps.text: Place the 2 eggs in the small saucepan and pour in cold water to cover them by 2–3 cm (about 500 ml).
steps.tip: Eggs straight from the fridge crack less if you start them in cold water like this.
steps.visualCue: Eggs lying flat on the bottom, fully under water
steps.cameraCheck: The eggs in the pan of water
steps.videoShot: Water being poured over two eggs in a saucepan.

steps.title: Bring to a boil
steps.text: Put the pan on high heat, uncovered.
steps.visualCue: Large bubbles rolling across the whole surface
steps.cameraCheck: The boiling water
steps.videoShot: Bubbles rising around the eggs.

steps.title: Cook the eggs
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, cover, and cook.
steps.tip: Chop the onion, tomato, ginger and garlic (steps 6–9) while the eggs cook.
steps.visualCue: Steady small bubbles; set a timer, as you cannot see doneness from outside
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan with the timer
steps.videoShot: A lid placed on the pan and a phone timer starting.

steps.title: Cool the eggs
steps.text: Drain the hot water and put the eggs in a bowl of cold water.
steps.visualCue: Eggs cool enough to hold comfortably
steps.cameraCheck: The eggs in cold water
steps.videoShot: Eggs being lifted with a spoon into a bowl of cold water.

steps.title: Peel the eggs
steps.text: Tap each egg all over on the counter, roll it gently, and peel off the shell under a little running water.
steps.tip: Torn whites are fine; they still taste the same in the curry.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, white eggs with no shell bits
steps.cameraCheck: The 2 peeled eggs on a plate
steps.videoShot: The shell coming away in large pieces.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 1 small onion (80 g).
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces, about ½ cup
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped onion on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the onion.

steps.title: Grate the ginger and garlic
steps.text: Grate ½-inch ginger (4 g) and 2 small garlic cloves (4 g). Finely chop 1 green chilli.
steps.visualCue: A small heap of wet, pale paste and chopped chilli
steps.cameraCheck: The ginger-garlic paste and chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: Ginger being rubbed on the grater.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop or grate 1 medium tomato (100 g).
steps.tip: Grating the tomato and leaving the skin in your hand gives a smoother gravy without a mixer.
steps.visualCue: A pulpy red heap, about ½ cup
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato in a bowl
steps.videoShot: A tomato half being grated, skin left behind.

steps.title: Measure the powders
steps.text: Put ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder and a pinch (about half the ⅛ tsp) turmeric in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: Three small coloured heaps in a bowl
steps.cameraCheck: The spice bowl
steps.videoShot: Spoons tipping powders into the bowl.

steps.title: Prick the eggs
steps.text: Make 6–8 small pricks all over each egg with a toothpick or fork (or make 2–3 shallow slits with a knife).
steps.tip: This stops the egg bursting in hot oil and lets the gravy soak in.
steps.visualCue: Tiny holes or slits in the white, yolk not exposed
steps.cameraCheck: A pricked egg
steps.videoShot: A fork pricking the egg.

steps.title: Season the eggs
steps.text: Rub the eggs with the remaining pinch of turmeric and a pinch of salt.
steps.visualCue: Evenly pale-yellow eggs
steps.cameraCheck: The yellow eggs on the plate
steps.videoShot: Fingers rolling an egg in turmeric.

steps.title: Heat 1 tsp oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat and add 1 tsp (5 ml) mustard oil. Heat until it just starts to smoke, then lower the heat.
steps.tip: Using a neutral oil? Just heat it until it shimmers; no need to smoke it.
steps.visualCue: A faint wisp of smoke, then the oil turns paler
steps.cameraCheck: The oil in the kadai
steps.videoShot: A thin wisp of smoke rising from the oil.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Add the eggs and roll them around on low-medium heat. Keep your face back: they may spit.
steps.tip: Optional step. If you skip it, keep this 1 tsp oil for step 14.
steps.visualCue: A light golden, slightly blistered skin all over
steps.cameraCheck: The golden eggs in the pan
steps.videoShot: Eggs rolling in the oil with a spoon.

steps.title: Take out the eggs and add the rest of the oil
steps.text: Lift the eggs onto the plate, leaving the oil behind. Add the second 1 tsp (5 ml) oil to the kadai.
steps.visualCue: Eggs out, oil shimmering
steps.cameraCheck: The eggs on the plate
steps.videoShot: The eggs being lifted out with a spoon.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add 1 bay leaf and ¼ tsp cumin seeds to the hot oil.
steps.tip: If the cumin turns black, it is burnt; wipe the pan and start again.
steps.visualCue: The cumin sizzles, darkens one shade and smells nutty; the bay leaf puffs
steps.cameraCheck: The sizzling cumin
steps.videoShot: Cumin dropping into oil and sizzling.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir on medium heat, stirring every 30 seconds.
steps.tip: This browning gives the dhaba taste. If the onion sticks, sprinkle 1 tsp water and scrape.
steps.visualCue: Soft, deep golden-brown onion with darker edges
steps.cameraCheck: The browned onion in the pan
steps.videoShot: The spatula turning golden onion.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Add the grated ginger-garlic and green chilli. Stir.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes and it smells sweet and fragrant
steps.cameraCheck: The paste mixed into the onion
steps.videoShot: The paste being stirred in.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the spice bowl powders and 1 tbsp water, and stir.
steps.tip: The splash of water stops the chilli powder from burning.
steps.visualCue: A dark red-brown paste; no dry powder visible
steps.cameraCheck: The spiced onion paste
steps.videoShot: Powders hitting the pan and the water splashing in.

steps.title: Add the tomato and salt
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and the remaining salt (about ¼ tsp). Raise the heat to medium and stir.
steps.visualCue: Bright red tomato mixed through the onion
steps.cameraCheck: The tomato in the pan
steps.videoShot: Tomato pulp tipping into the masala.

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.text: Cook, stirring and mashing the tomato with the spatula.
steps.tip: Adding curd (optional)? Lower the heat, stir in the whisked curd now and cook 1–2 more minutes until oil shows again.
steps.visualCue: The tomato breaks down into a thick, jammy paste and small drops of oil appear at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: Oil glistening at the edge of the masala
steps.videoShot: Close-up of oil separating at the edge.

steps.title: Add hot water
steps.text: Pour in 150 ml (⅔ cup) hot water and stir well.
steps.tip: Hot water keeps the gravy boiling and the flavour deeper than cold water.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, orange-red gravy, about as thick as pouring cream
steps.cameraCheck: The gravy in the pan
steps.videoShot: Water being poured and stirred in.

steps.title: Bring to a boil
steps.text: Let the gravy come to a boil on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Bubbles all over the surface
steps.cameraCheck: The bubbling gravy
steps.videoShot: Gravy bubbling.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Slide in the 2 eggs. Spoon gravy over them.
steps.tip: You can halve the eggs lengthwise instead, but add the halves yolk-up at the very end so the yolk does not dissolve.
steps.visualCue: Eggs half covered with gravy
steps.cameraCheck: The eggs in the curry
steps.videoShot: Eggs being lowered into the gravy.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low heat. Turn the eggs once halfway.
steps.tip: Taste the gravy now and fix the salt.
steps.visualCue: The gravy thickens slightly and the eggs turn orange-red on the outside
steps.cameraCheck: The simmering curry with the lid lifted
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting to show glossy gravy and eggs.

steps.title: Add garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle ¼ tsp garam masala and crush ½ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the curry. Stir gently.
steps.visualCue: Flecks of green and a strong, warm smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi on the curry
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Finish and rest
steps.text: Turn off the heat, scatter 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves, and rest the curry covered. Remove the bay leaf before eating.
steps.visualCue: A thin red oil layer on top and green coriander flecks
steps.cameraCheck: The finished curry in a bowl
steps.videoShot: The curry ladled into a bowl with both eggs on top.

reasons: two eggs give about 15–16 g of complete protein plus vitamin B12, choline and vitamin D, and the gravy is onion, tomato and spices with only 2 tsp of oil; nothing is deep-fried and there is no cream or sugar. Points come off for only modest vegetables and fibre, sodium around 900 mg, and the yolks' cholesterol for people told to limit it. Restaurant versions commonly use 2–4 times the oil, add butter, cream or cashew paste, salt more heavily and come with naan or a large mound of rice.

researchRating.basis: egg curry is one of India's most-cooked everyday non-veg dishes and a dhaba staple; Swasthi's Recipes' dhaba-style egg curry shows 4.98/5 from 485 votes, Archana's Kitchen's Punjabi egg curry shows a ratings count of about 9,000, and celebrity chefs (Ranveer Brar, with several versions) and major blogs (Whisk Affair, My Food Story, Cook With Kushi) all publish it. Swiggy's Mumbai page lists about 50 egg curry dishes, showing wide availability. Small deduction because some people find it plain compared with meat curries and the eggs can turn rubbery if overcooked.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days; cool it within 1 hour of cooking. Freezing is not recommended: boiled egg whites turn rubbery and watery after freezing (the gravy alone, without eggs, freezes for up to 1 month). Reheat in a pan on low heat with 1–2 tbsp water, covered, until it bubbles, about 3–4 minutes; or microwave covered in 30-second bursts. Halve the eggs before microwaving so they do not burst.
leftoverRemix: egg curry masala toast / anda ghotala. Chop the leftover eggs roughly, then cook them with the leftover gravy in a pan until thick and almost dry. Spread the mixture on toasted pav or bread, top with chopped onion, coriander and a little grated cheese, and toast it closed like a sandwich or eat it open. The thick masala turns into a quick spicy Mumbai-style egg toast.
burnOff: about 4.5 km of running (315 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.3 km of brisk walking (about 1 hour 15 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 495 kcal): about 7.1 km running or 9.9 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: contains egg, onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided in the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains egg, onion and garlic, which the common Ekadashi rule set avoids (same rules as Navratri vrat in the sources used).

jain.reason: contains egg plus onion, garlic and ginger (root vegetables).

ramadan.reason: egg needs no halal meat sourcing and gives slow, filling protein; for sehri keep salt and chilli moderate so it does not cause thirst during the fast.
